games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: What does the word “breath” mean?
choices: A small amount of water in the air or on a surface.
The air you take in and let out of your lungs.
Small balls of ice that fall from the sky during a storm.
A large field of grass and flowers where animals graze.
rounds.answer: The air you take in and let out of your lungs.
rounds.explanation: Breath is the air your lungs take in and let out, as in “I took a deep breath”.

rounds.prompt: What does the word “canyon” mean?
choices: A part of the sea or a lake that is partly surrounded by land.
The soft hair that covers some animals' bodies.
Covered with, or full of, snow.
A deep valley with steep sides, often with a river at the bottom.
rounds.answer: A deep valley with steep sides, often with a river at the bottom.
rounds.explanation: A canyon is a deep valley with steep sides, which is why it is deeper than a meadow.

rounds.prompt: Choose the missing word from “The Storm and the Science Tent”: Nora sat down, catching her _____.
rounds.explanation: Nora had just run to the hall, so she sat down catching her breath.

rounds.prompt: Choose the missing word from “Weather Around the World”: Rain helps plants grow, because plants need _____.
rounds.explanation: The text explains that rain matters to plants because plants need moisture.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses the comparative form correctly?
choices: A hurricane is strong than a storm.
A hurricane is stronger than a storm.
A hurricane is most strong than a storm.
A hurricane is the strongest than a storm.
rounds.answer: A hurricane is stronger than a storm.
rounds.explanation: One-syllable adjectives add -er, and than joins the two things being compared.

rounds.prompt: Complete the sentence: This is _____ morning of the year.
rounds.explanation: Foggy ends in -y, so it becomes foggiest, and a superlative needs the in front of it.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: In “Weather Around the World”, why do plants need moisture?
choices: Plants need moisture to grow, and the rain gives them that water.
A gentle storm brings rain, but a hurricane brings very strong wind.
Amal says a tornado spins faster than any other storm.
rounds.answer: Plants need moisture to grow, and the rain gives them that water.
rounds.explanation: The text joins the two ideas with because: rain helps plants grow, because plants need moisture.

rounds.prompt: What difference does the text give between a gentle storm and a hurricane?
choices: The poem uses still, quiet and slow to show the calm.
Stronger compares two things, and most powerful compares many things.
A gentle storm brings rain, but a hurricane brings very strong wind.
rounds.answer: A gentle storm brings rain, but a hurricane brings very strong wind.
rounds.explanation: The writer contrasts the two with but, so the hurricane is clearly the more powerful weather.

rounds.prompt: Why does the poet say the hills have almost gone away?
choices: They planned to teach how storms work and how people can stay safe.
The fog is so thick that the hills cannot be seen from below.
The poem uses still, quiet and slow to show the calm.
rounds.answer: The fog is so thick that the hills cannot be seen from below.
rounds.explanation: The hills have not moved; the last line explains that the whole world hides in fog.

rounds.prompt: What does the reporter tell listeners to do when they hear thunder, and why?
choices: Go inside and stay calm, because thunder warns that the storm is close.
The fog is so thick that the hills cannot be seen from below.
The wind picked up and the surface of the lake began to ripple.
rounds.answer: Go inside and stay calm, because thunder warns that the storm is close.
rounds.explanation: The safety line comes straight after the storm forecast, so the advice belongs to that storm.

rounds.prompt: Nora says “stronger” and “most powerful”. Which one compares only two things?
choices: The report says the storm may bring rain and hail tonight.
She sat catching her breath, her heart was beating fast and her shirt was wet with sweat.
Stronger compares two things, and most powerful compares many things.
rounds.answer: Stronger compares two things, and most powerful compares many things.
rounds.explanation: Stronger is a comparative, so it needs two items; most powerful is a superlative for a whole group.

rounds.prompt: What happened to the lake just before the storm returned?
choices: Plants need moisture to grow, and the rain gives them that water.
The wind picked up and the surface of the lake began to ripple.
Go inside and stay calm, because thunder warns that the storm is close.
rounds.answer: The wind picked up and the surface of the lake began to ripple.
rounds.explanation: The ripple is the warning sign; the shout about the storm comes in the next paragraph.
